subject: predicting detection probabilities with a large dataset

messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: predicting detection probabilities with a large dataset
parts:
I've been trying to generate detection probabilities from occu and
colext models (i.e., predict(model,type="det")) and am having some
issues.

Using an single-season occu model (1,000 sites, 4 observations, 4 site-
level predictors, 4 observation-level predictors), my newer,
reasonably fast machine has taken over an hour (and is still running)
to generate these predictions, while predictions on a two-season
colext model (same parameters, but now 8 observations [4 obs, 2
seasons]) results a error to the effect that a vector of 2.8 Gb cannot
be allocated, even when freeing up as much memory as possible and
setting memory limits to 4 Gb.

I have had no issues in running the models, nor in generating
predictions for state, psi, col, and ext; though more parameters =
longer processing as expected (rarely over 30 seconds). I didn't
think I was asking too much of unmarked/R, but maybe I am. Are there
any suggested methods for getting predict() to get the job done?

With gratitude for the unmarked package,

Giancarlo

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] predicting detection probabilities with a large dataset
parts:
Hi Giancarlo,

This is probably an issue related to the calculation of SEs using the delta method in linearComb(). Note that predict (source code is here) is basically just a wrapper around linearComb() and backTransform(), so you could try to use them directly.  Don't have time to dig into it now, but an alternative is get your predictions this way:

oc <- obsCovs(yourUMF)
X <- model.matrix(~cov1 + cov2 + etc..., oc) # design matrix
betas <- coef(yourFittedModel, type="det")
p <- plogis(X %*% betas)

If you want SEs and CIs, you could apply the delta method yourself, or use either nonparboot or parboot.

Hope this helps,
Richard
